situation:
You are the human resources director at HARBOR REACH FAMILY SERVICES, a nonprofit agency that runs counseling, housing assistance and youth programs across a mid-sized county. The board chair (judge) has asked to meet with you privately about who should lead the agency's programs when the current director of programs retires this spring.

HARBOR REACH FAMILY SERVICES was formed eighteen months ago when two long-standing agencies combined. The merger agreement committed the board to filling leadership openings with equal consideration for staff from each side, and much of the work of blending the two staffs is unfinished. Caseworkers from the smaller of the two agencies still introduce themselves by their former employer's name.

Two internal candidates are strong. One is a program supervisor who came from the larger legacy agency and already oversees most of the combined caseload. The other came from the smaller agency and built the housing program the county now depends on. Neither has been told they are under consideration, and the board has kept the search confidential. Opening the position to outside applicants remains possible.

Promoting either supervisor gives one group of caseworkers the recognition they have waited eighteen months for and confirms the other group's fear that the merger was an absorption; the supervisor who is passed over may leave, and staff loyal to that supervisor may follow. Going outside treats both sides evenly, but it fills the position after the retirement date with someone who knows neither program's history.

The board chair (judge) wants you to analyze the factors the board should weigh, recommend how the position should be filled, and explain how the internal candidates and the wider staff should be handled while the decision is being made. The board chair (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the board chair (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the board chair (judge) at HARBOR REACH FAMILY SERVICES. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the human resources director to recommend whether the director of programs position should go to one of the two internal supervisors or be opened to outside applicants, to say what that choice costs the staff on each side of the merger, and to explain how the candidates and the wider staff should be treated while the search stays confidential.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: Six months from now, what would tell us we got this right?
If caseworkers from one side start resigning, does that mean we chose wrong?
